findings.message: Launching ".NET API: Debug" on its own (root launch.json or backend workspace) stops the Docker exp container and starts nothing on port 5002, so the API it launches cannot fetch its startup config from EXP_PROXY_URL=http://localhost:5002. launch.json:62 sets preLaunchTask "Build: API for Debug". In tasks.json that task has dependsOn ["Infra: Setup Docker"], which runs `npm run dev:local:setup` → scripts/dev-local.ts --setup-only. main() always calls swapExpToBareMetalMode(), which runs `docker stop exp-arolariu-ro`, and BARE_METAL_SERVICES["setup-only"] is []. The config itself sets EXP_PROXY_URL to http://localhost:5002, and AddProxyConfiguration fetches Auth:JWT:Secret and the other keys at startup. Only the compound also starts exp. DEVELOPMENT.md still lists ".NET API: Debug" as a standalone profile.

Keep exp available during API debugger setup The API debug profile runs `dev:local:setup`, which unconditionally stops Docker exp but starts no replacement in `setup-only` mode. Consequently, launching the API debugger alone leaves its configured `http://localhost:5002` dependency unavailable. In the full-stack compound, setup can also stop Docker exp after the Python debugger has already attempted to bind its occupied port. Ensure exp startup and port release are ordered before launching its consumers.

Each orchestrator run starts the Docker exp container again with `docker compose up -d` before stopping it. In the Full Stack compound the bare-metal exp launches at the same time as this preLaunchTask, so both may race for host port 5002 and either uvicorn or the compose step can fail. startStorage() runs `docker compose -f Storage/docker-compose.yml up -d`. That compose file defines service exp (container exp-arolariu-ro, ports "5002:80", with a build section), so it is started or built on every run. swapExpToBareMetalMode() stops it only afterwards. In the compounds (launch.json "Full Stack: Website + API + exp" and fullstack.code-workspace), "Python: exp FastAPI Debug" has no preLaunchTask and binds 127.0.0.1:5002 while the API's preLaunchTask is still running this sequence. If dockerCompose() throws, main() exits 1 and the API debug session never starts.

The Azurite readiness probe may never return a 2xx response, because it sends an unauthenticated account-level list request. Every `dev:local` run and every debug preLaunchTask would then wait the full 60s timeout, which contradicts the documented ~3-second preLaunchTask. waitForHealth("http://localhost:10000/devstoreaccount1?comp=list", ...) treats only `response.ok` as healthy and sends no Authorization or SAS. Azurite runs with `--oauth basic`, and an anonymous account-level List Containers call is rejected unless public access applies. The compose healthcheck for Azurite uses only a TCP connect. DEVELOPMENT.md says: "If Docker infra is already running, the preLaunchTask completes in ~3 seconds."

Use an authenticated or TCP readiness check for Azurite The blob-service list request requires authorization, so a healthy Azurite instance returns 403 to this unsigned fetch. Since `waitForHealth` accepts only successful responses, every local startup and debugger setup waits the full 60-second timeout and reports storage as unhealthy. Use a TCP probe like the Compose healthcheck, or an authenticated SDK request.

The Azurite init swallows every error inside the child script, so the orchestrator reports "Azurite blob containers initialized with CORS" even when container creation or the CORS setup failed. The `node -e` script ends with `.catch(()=>{})`, so the child always exits 0. The surrounding try/catch therefore never reaches logWarning, and logSuccess runs unconditionally. The original selfhost-start.sh at least printed `e.message`.

The inline Azurite init script ends with `.catch(()=>{})`, so the node process always exits 0. The script then always logs 'Azurite blob containers initialized with CORS', even when the container or CORS setup failed (for example, Azurite not ready yet). Let the error reach the exit code so the warning branch can actually run. The inline Azurite init script ends with `.catch(()=>{})`, so the node process always exits 0. The new script hardcodes the MSSQL SA password and the Azurite account key in source, adding another copy of the credential to keep in sync. Line 145 runs `sqlcmd ... -U sa -P "qazWSXedcRFV1234!"` and the Azurite connection string embeds AccountKey=Eby8vdM02x.... These are local-emulator values that already appear in infra/Local/Storage/docker-comp.yml (MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD) and in selfhost-start.sh. selfhost-start.sh reads the password from $MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD, while this script uses a literal.

Whether Entra ID auth is used now depends on an exact string match of the URL rather than on the Azure identity. An EXP_PROXY_URL such as "https://exp.arolariu.ro/" (trailing slash) or any other Azure-hosted exp URL silently drops the bearer token. The .NET side, which does not trim, behaves differently from the TS side, which does. configProxy.ts: `const USE_AZURE_AUTH = EXP_BASE_URL === AZURE_EXP_URL;` after `process.env["EXP_PROXY_URL"]?.trim() || ...`. generate.env.ts has the same logic. WebApplicationBuilderExtensions.cs:122: `var useAzureAuth = baseUrl == ConfigProxyUrlAzure;` with `explicitUrl` taken untrimmed from Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable. Before this change, auth was keyed on AZURE_CLIENT_ID being present.

Placing the new "Development" profile first makes it the default for `dotnet run`/`dotnet watch run`. Every default local launch therefore now forces EXP_PROXY_URL=http://localhost:5002 and HTTP on :5000, replacing the previous "Console App" default (HTTPS, no exp override). "Development" is inserted before "Console App" in profiles, and the dotnet CLI uses the first Project profile when --launch-profile is absent. Its environmentVariables set EXP_PROXY_URL and INFRA, so any developer whose exp runs only in Docker (http://exp) now gets an API pointed at localhost:5002.

The new "Development" profile is now the first one in the file, and `dotnet run`/`dotnet watch run` use the first profile by default. So every plain local `dotnet run` now sets EXP_PROXY_URL=http://localhost:5002, INFRA=local and binds to http://localhost:5000. That replaces the previous default ("Console App"). Anyone running the API against Docker exp (http://exp) or Azure exp will be silently sent to localhost:5002 and Entra auth will be skipped. Make this profile opt-in with `--launch-profile Development`, or keep it out of the first position. The new exp test and lint targets pip-install into whatever Python interpreter is active, with no virtualenv, on every run. Because the root `npm run test` / `test:unit` use `run-many --all`, these targets may now run in workflows that never set up Python. The test target command is `python -m pip install -q -r requirements-dev.txt && python -m pytest -q` (lint is similar). The root package.json has "test": "nx run-many --target=test --all" and "test:unit": "nx run-many --target=test --configuration=unit --all". .github/scripts/src/hygiene/checks/testCheck.ts runs `npm run test:unit`. The exp target defines no `unit` configuration. The new pinned dev dependencies (pytest==9.0.2, ruff==0.15.4) are installed this way.

The `test` and `lint` targets run `python -m pip install -q -r requirements-dev.txt` on every run, into whatever interpreter is first on PATH (often the global or user site-packages, not a venv). This has side effects, is slow, and can fail on externally managed Python installs (PEP 668). `npm run test` (run-many) now triggers it for everyone. Install dependencies in a separate setup step or a venv instead. The script's own usage docs and one branch disagree with what it does: --frontend and --infra also start exp, and the "Infrastructure-only mode" branch can never run. The header says `--frontend  # Start infra + website only` and `--infra  # Start infra only (no services)`. However, BARE_METAL_SERVICES has frontend: ["exp","website"] and infra: ["exp"]. `if (bareMetalServices.length === 0)` is true only for "setup-only", so the else branch that prints "Infrastructure-only mode. Start services manually" is dead code. Step 2 also logs "Starting databases (... exp)" just before the script stops exp.

The new endpoint and auth selection logic, which decides whether config requests carry a bearer token, ships without any test in the .NET API, the website or generate.env.ts. The diff changes the baseUrl and useAzureAuth logic in AddProxyConfiguration, and EXP_BASE_URL/USE_AZURE_AUTH in configProxy.ts and generate.env.ts. It adds no test file: the only test-related additions are the exp nx targets and requirements-dev.txt.

The diff includes unrelated French translation additions in a dev-tooling change and drops the file's trailing newline. The fr.json hunks add insufficientData, saving, error/success, totalDuration, minutes, none, emptyState, unknownMerchant and andMore keys (already present in en.json and ro.json), and end with `\ No newline at end of file`. Separately, devcontainer.json's new postStartCommand runs `npm run generate 2>/dev/null || true` on every container start. That may regenerate tracked files like these, and any failure is hidden.

This PR also makes unrelated French translation changes that aren't in the description, and it removes the file's trailing newline. The `exp:dev` target (`python -m uvicorn ...`) and the debugpy launch config will fail with 'No module named uvicorn'. That breaks the default dev:local profile, which always starts exp. postStartCommand now runs the full `npm run generate` (env, i18n, GraphQL) on every container start, and sends stderr to /dev/null. generate:env tries to fetch config from exp (http://exp by default, which won't resolve in the container), so each start can stall until a timeout, and real generation failures are hidden. Services are started with `spawn(..., {shell: true})`, and shutdown calls `p.kill()`. That only signals the intermediate shell, not the npx/nx → dotnet watch / uvicorn / next process tree. On SIGTERM (for example, when VS Code stops the task), the real dev servers can be left orphaned and keep holding ports 3000/5000/5002. That causes the 'port already in use' problem the docs describe. Spawn detached and kill the process group, or drop `shell: true`. When any one service exits (for example, exp crashes because Python deps are missing), `Promise.race` resolves and `main` returns. The other children keep running, nothing reports which service died, and the exit code isn't passed on. The orchestrator ends up in a half-running state with no clear failure message. "Build: API for Debug" depends on "Infra: Setup Docker" (dev-local --setup-only), and that task calls process.exit(1) when Docker isn't running. As a result, the plain ".NET API: Debug" launch (root, backend and fullstack workspaces) can't start at all without Docker. Debugging the API on its own, for example to test startup, no longer works. Consider a separate debug profile that doesn't require infra.
